rationale: The cellar motion sensor (SEN-D1) shows RSSI -83 dBm, below the -80 dBm threshold that causes intermittent disconnections and missed alerts. It is located behind thick concrete walls with the base station two floors up, while all other devices are online and the base station is healthy. Moving the sensor closer to the base station made it stay online and trigger alerts reliably, confirming weak signal as the root cause.

repair_steps: Guide the customer to permanently relocate the cellar motion sensor (SEN-D1) to a location with better signal, such as upstairs or closer to the base station, ensuring RSSI is above -80 dBm.
If relocation is not feasible, recommend installing the official RP-1 repeater between the base station and the cellar to boost signal strength.
After the fix, verify the sensor's RSSI in Device Settings > Device Info and confirm it stays online and triggers alerts reliably over a period of time.

results.text: Peripherals talk to the base station over a sub-GHz proprietary radio. Signal strength (RSSI) is shown in Device Settings > Device Info. Above -70 dBm is good, -70 to -80 dBm is acceptable, below -80 dBm causes intermittent disconnections, delayed notifications and choppy live view. Concrete walls, metal doors and fridges strongly attenuate the signal. Fix: move the device or base station, or install the official RP-1 repeater.
